direct_answer: Aker BP states that it does not have a climate transition plan in line with ESRS requirements because it has no targets to reduce Scope 3 emissions, and it also states it does not have a timeline for developing such a plan [Source 1]. Therefore, a 1.5°C alignment of a transition plan is not applicable / not demonstrated in the disclosed information [Source 1]. While Aker BP uses IEA scenario analysis including a 1.5°C-aligned Net Zero Emissions (NZE) scenario, this is described as stress testing portfolio resilience rather than a company transition plan aligned to 1.5°C [Sources 2, 5].
compliance_rationale: The company explicitly discloses that it does not have a climate transition plan in line with ESRS requirements and provides the reason (no Scope 3 reduction targets) and confirms there is no timeline to develop such a plan [Source 1]. This directly answers whether a transition plan exists and implies that 1.5°C alignment of such a plan cannot be claimed based on the disclosures [Source 1].
disclosure_gaps: Any description of an ESRS-compliant climate transition plan (actions, resources, governance, milestones) is absent because the company states it does not have one [Source 1].
Explicit statement/assessment that a transition plan is aligned with 1.5°C (or not aligned), including methodology/criteria for alignment, is not provided [Source 1].
Scope 3 emissions reduction targets (a stated prerequisite in their explanation) are not disclosed in the transition plan section; instead, the absence of such targets is noted [Source 1].
key_findings: Aker BP discloses it does not have a climate transition plan in line with ESRS requirements and has no timeline to develop one, citing lack of Scope 3 reduction targets [Source 1].
Aker BP conducts scenario analysis using IEA World Energy Outlook scenarios, including an NZE scenario described as a 1.5°C pathway, to test portfolio resilience [Sources 2, 5].
